Southwest of the region, a tropical disturbance, Invest 99W, is 
within a developing monsoon pattern in Yap State. The Marianas
remain in the northern periphery of this unsettled pattern with
only scattered showers moving across Guam this afternoon. Depending 
on the development and a gradual northwestward track of 99W, showers 
are expected to build across the converging monsoon and trade-wind 
patterns in its wake, bringing scattered to numerous locally heavy 
showers and isolated thunderstorms to the Marianas by midweek. 
Convectively-driven gusts to 25 mph are expected with heavier 
showers, with hi-res model guidance suggesting occasional gusts to 30
mph. Although there still remains some uncertainty in this outcome, 
where the actual speed, strength, and track of 99W will determine how
close in proximity the trailing convergence is to the Marianas. 

Marine/Surf...
Gentle to moderate easterly trade winds begin to increase Tuesday,
becoming gentle to fresh and shifting southeast by Wednesday. 
Combined seas of 3 to 5 feet are gradually increasing due with the
arrival of a longer period north swell. Southwest swell is 
expected to fill in towards the latter half of the week, building
seas to 6 to 8 feet. A moderate risk of rip currents continues along
east facing reefs of the Marianas through at least Thursday. Longer-
period north swell is moving through the region, bringing a moderate
risk of rip currents along north-facing reefs Tuesday. The arrival of
southwest swell may slightly increase surf along west and south 
facing reefs, potentially bringing a moderate rip risk as well.
However, this is dependent on the development of the tropical 
disturbance in Yap State.

Tropical Systems...
Invest 99W is gradually developing a low-level circulation and is
currently rated as a "LOW" by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center 
(JTWC). This means that development is still possible, but 
significant tropical cyclone development is unlikely within 24 hours.
99W is loosely centered near 8N141E, northwest of Woleai, and north
of Sorol in Yap State, and is embedded in a developing monsoon 
pattern. Although largely disorganized, there is a broad area of 
flaring, deep convection further developing along the monsoon surge 
south-southeast of the disturbance. Additionally, a band of numerous
to widespread showers have developed along the northern and eastern 
peripheries of the disturbance due to converging trade-wind flow. 

99W looks to gradually become more organized over the next few days,
merging with a weaker monsoon disturbance near Palau as it drifts 
west-northwest towards Yap Proper, potentially lifting northward 
around midweek with a monsoon tail developing on the south side. The
latest guidance continues to show 99W become more organized as it
lifts northward. This will allow the westerlies to intensify within
the monsoon tail, impacting Palau and Yap, and the southerlies to
intensify in the inflow tail, potentially impacting the Marianas.
Invest 99W will produce locally heavy rainfall, gusty winds, and
choppy seas over the next several days. 

For more information on Invest 99W, see bulletins issued by JTWC 
under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
The bulk of activity in the region is south of Pohnpei where a 
portion of the Near Equatorial Trough (NET) and an embedded, weakening
tropical disturbance interact. The most recent frames of visible 
satellite imagery show a band of increasing shower coverage and 
moderate convection where the northern peripheries of said
disturbance converge with trade-wind flow from the northeast. Due to
the fairly quick northward shift of this band as depicted in models,
PoPs for Pohnpei tonight remain at 40 percent with isolated 
thunderstorms expected. As for Kosrae and Majuro, PoPs are expected 
to be lower as Precipitable Water (PWAT) values of 2.3 inches or less
are advected downstream. A fragmented, weak ITCZ is producing some 
trade-wind troughs within the region, but this feature is expected to
remain minor for the next few days. As we enter the latter half of 
the week, an increase in showers and thunderstorms across all three 
forecast points is possible due to an active ITCZ from the central 
Pacific entering eastern Micronesia.

Overall sea state remains steady with combined seas of 4 to 6 feet
across Pohnpei and Kosrae and up to 7 feet near Majuro. Light to 
gentle easterly winds prevail across the entire region. Gusts will be
stronger near thunderstorms within coastal waters. A minor north 
swell is expected to spread across the region on Wednesday, 
potentially increasing surf along north-facing reefs. Combined seas, 
however, should remain below hazardous levels.

Western Micronesia...
Satellite imagery shows scattered to widespread showers across the 
region with scattered showers seen across Yap Proper and Chuuk, and 
numerous showers across Palau. Altimetry shows combined seas between 
4 and 6 feet.
